The residue of $ e^{1/z} $ at $ z=0 $ is the coefficient of the $ \frac{1}{z} $ term in its Laurent series expansion. Expanding $ e^{1/z} $ as $ \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n! z^n} $, the term with $ \frac{1}{z} $ corresponds to $ n=1 $, giving a coefficient of $ \frac{1}{1!} = 1 $.
